gl.4-20mA: A common smooth signal: 4 mA means the lowest value, 20 mA the highest.
gl.CPO: Crude palm oil: the mill's main product.
gl.DOSH: Malaysia's Department of Occupational Safety and Health.
gl.EFB: Empty fruit bunch: what is left after the fruit is removed.
gl.ERP: Business software for orders, stock and accounts.
gl.FAT: Factory acceptance test: proving the system works before delivery.
gl.FBD: Function block diagram: a PLC style that connects ready-made blocks.
gl.FFB: Fresh fruit bunches: the palm fruit that arrives at the mill.
gl.HMI: The screen an operator uses to watch and control one machine.
gl.I/O: Inputs and outputs: what a PLC senses (buttons, sensors) and controls (motors, lamps).
gl.IIoT: Industrial internet of things: connected factory sensors and machines.
gl.LAD: Ladder: a PLC programming style that looks like an electrical wiring drawing.
gl.Ladder: A PLC programming style that looks like an electrical wiring drawing.
gl.MCC: Motor control centre: the cabinet that powers the plant's motors.
gl.MES: Software that plans and tracks production on the factory floor.
gl.MQTT: A lightweight messaging method often used to send factory data to dashboards.
gl.Modbus: A simple, widely used way for machines to exchange numbers.
gl.NPN: A sensor wiring type that switches to 0 V. It must match the PLC input wiring.
gl.OER: Oil extraction rate: how much oil the mill gets from the fruit.
gl.OPC UA: A modern standard way for industrial systems to share data securely.
gl.PAC: A more powerful industrial controller, used for large or critical plants.
gl.PID: Automatic control that holds a value steady, like cruise control in a car.
gl.PLC: A tough little computer that controls machines by following written rules.
gl.PNP: A sensor wiring type that switches to +24 V. Common on modern PLC inputs.
gl.POME: Palm oil mill effluent: the mill's waste water, which must be treated.
gl.RS-232: An old serial cable link between two devices.
gl.RS-485: A serial cable link shared by several devices on one line.
gl.RTD: A temperature sensor whose resistance changes with heat.
gl.SAT: Site acceptance test: proving the system works once installed on site.
gl.SCADA: Control-room software that watches the whole plant, with alarms and charts.
gl.SFC: Sequential function chart: a PLC style for step-by-step sequences.
gl.SIL: Safety integrity level: how reliable a safety function must be.
gl.SQLite: A small database kept in a single file.
gl.VFD: A motor drive that sets how fast a motor turns.
gl.analog: A signal that changes smoothly, like temperature, instead of just on or off.
gl.historian: A database that records machine values over time.
gl.interlock: A rule that blocks an action unless something else is safe or ready.
gl.latch: A memory that stays on after the button is released.
gl.permissive: A condition that must be true before a machine is allowed to start.
gl.setpoint: The target value, such as the temperature you want.
gl.watchdog: A timer that stops the PLC safely if the program gets stuck.

rc.sum1: No single licence makes someone a machine-safety assessor everywhere.
rc.sum2: Competence mixes standards training, machine experience and review by qualified engineers.
rc.sum3: This page shows training options, typical costs and what a good assessment produces.
rc.title: Becoming safety qualified
rc.when.like: Re-checking a building after adding a new floor.
rc.when.plain: Check the risks before installing, changing or buying a used machine. Changing code or speed can make an old check out of date.
rc.when.title: When to check machine risks
rc.where.like: A first-aid class versus a nursing degree.
rc.where.plain: Training ranges from short local courses to recognised certificates such as CMSE, TUV or exida. Pick one that fits your machines and job.
rc.where.title: Where to get trained
sa.a1: A certified PLC or safety controller, not a hobby board.
sa.a2: Drawings, wiring, settings, testing and training, not the hardware itself.
sa.a3: Spotting unusual motor current, or checking fruit quality with a camera.
sa.cyber.like: Locking the factory gate, not just the office door.
sa.cyber.plain: Connecting machines to networks adds risk. Keep networks separate, use proper passwords and control remote access.
sa.cyber.title: Keeping connected machines secure
sa.edge-ai.like: A helpful assistant, not the person holding the brake.
sa.edge-ai.plain: AI can help spot problems, check quality and save energy. It must never replace safety trips or secretly control machines.
sa.edge-ai.title: What AI should and should not do
sa.install.like: Moving house takes longer than buying the furniture.
sa.install.plain: Setting up a system takes longer than buying it. Most time goes on drawings, wiring, settings and testing.
sa.install.title: Where setup time really goes
sa.lead: Factories mix different controllers. This lesson shows which one suits which job, budget and risk.
sa.matrix.like: Choosing between a van, a lorry, a car and a bicycle.
sa.matrix.plain: Four kinds of controller are compared: WECON PLCs, PAC systems, Raspberry Pi and Arduino. Each is best at a different job.
sa.matrix.title: Four kinds of controller compared

sa.reliability.like: A good car still needs fuel, servicing and a spare tyre.
sa.reliability.plain: Reliable systems need clean power, cool cabinets, spare parts and backups. The controller alone is not enough.
sa.reliability.title: What keeps a system reliable
sa.safety: Use certified controllers for machine control and safety.
sa.scale.like: A home kitchen versus a restaurant chain.
sa.scale.plain: The same mill idea needs different tools at different sizes. A hobby project, a small plant and a large group each need more engineering.
sa.scale.title: Small, medium and large mills
sa.standards-stack.like: A road-sign guide for factory rules.
sa.standards-stack.plain: A quick guide to the standard names you will hear. Each row says what area it covers and what to do first.
sa.standards-stack.title: Standard names in one table
sa.sum1: Factories mix PLCs, PACs, Raspberry Pi and Arduino-style boards.
sa.sum2: Certified PLCs handle control and safety. Small boards suit data, learning and prototypes.
sa.sum3: Choose each device by its job, budget and risk, not by brand.
